propositions.text: The applicant seeks to set aside the FPSLREB decision in Treasury Board v. Association of Justice Counsel, 2020 FPSLREB 59.
propositions.quote: The applicant seeks to set aside the decision of an adjudicator of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations and Employment Board (the FPSLREB) in Treasury Board (Department of Justice) v. Association of Justice Counsel, 2020 FPSLREB 59.

propositions.text: The FPSLREB decision excluded the LP-04 position in the CILP from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.
propositions.quote: In that decision, the adjudicator determined that the LP-04 position in the Centre for Information Law and Privacy (CILP) within the Department of Justice should be excluded from the bargaining unit under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations Act, S.C. 2003, c. 22, s. 2 (the FPSLRA).

propositions.text: The adjudicator found the incumbent provided advice on issues under the Privacy Act and the Access to Information Act, creating a conflict of interest.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator determined that the incumbent of the position in question was sometimes called upon to provide advice on issues under the Privacy Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-21 and the Access to Information Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. A-1 in the context of labour relations-sensitive matters.

propositions.text: The adjudicator concluded there was a sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing, and classification matters to justify exclusion due to conflict of interest.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator concluded at paragraph 39 of his reasons that there was accordingly a “sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification matters” to justify the exclusion due to the potential for a conflict of interest under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: The adjudicator did not find exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) was warranted as the occupant did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing, or classification issues.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator, however, determined that an exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) of the FPSLRA was not warranted as the occupant of the position did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing or classification issues, themselves.

propositions.text: The applicant argues the adjudicator's interpretation of the statutory provisions was unreasonable and too broad.
propositions.quote: First, the applicant says that the adjudicator unreasonably interpreted the relevant statutory provisions, which should be read narrowly as they limit the constitutionally-protected right to join and be represented by a trade union.

propositions.text: The applicant claims the interpretation broadens the scope of labour relations exclusions beyond what Parliament intended.
propositions.quote: The applicant submits that the text, context and purpose of the relevant provisions indicate that Parliament contemplated that all labour relations-related exclusions would fall under either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA and that it was therefore not reasonable to interpret paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Act as including duties in relations to labour relations matters that do not rise to the level of being covered by either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: The applicant asserts the adjudicator's decision was unreasonable because it relied on the incumbent's seniority, which is irrelevant.
propositions.quote: The applicant says that, were it otherwise, no senior government lawyer could ever be unionized, which was clearly not the intent of Parliament when it extended collective bargaining rights to lawyers working for the federal government in 2005.

propositions.text: The court disagrees with the applicant's interpretation and finds the adjudicator's interpretation reasonable.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator’s interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA was therefore reasonable.

propositions.text: The court also finds the adjudicator did not unreasonably base his decision on the incumbent's seniority.
propositions.quote: The comments made by the adjudicator in paragraphs 42 and 43 of his reasons that the applicant points to must be read in context and are responsive to suggestions that the employer could have ensured all labour relations-sensitive discussions were held with the more junior excluded lawyer in the CILP.

propositions.text: The court dismisses the application and upholds the FPSLREB decision, with costs.
propositions.quote: I would accordingly dismiss this application, with costs, fixed in the agreed-upon all-inclusive amount of $2,500.00, which I believe to be reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court reviewed the applicant's challenge to the FPSLREB decision excluding a position from the bargaining unit, and upheld the decision, rejecting the applicant's arguments.

propositions.text: The adjudicator determined that the incumbent provided advice on privacy and access to information, creating a conflict of interest.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator concluded at paragraph 39 of his reasons that there was accordingly a “sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification matters” to justify the exclusion due to the potential for a conflict of interest under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: The adjudicator found that advice on privacy and access to information did not warrant exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c).
propositions.quote: the adjudicator, however, determined that an exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) of the FPSLRA was not warranted as the occupant of the position did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing or classification issues, themselves.

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator found the incumbent's advice on privacy and access issues created a conflict of interest, justifying exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(g).

propositions.text: The relevant provisions in the FPSLRA allow the employer to apply for exclusion of positions providing advice on labour relations, staffing, or classification.
propositions.quote: The relevant provisions in the FPSLRA provide: Application Demande 59 (1) ... the employer may apply to the Board for an order declaring that any position of an employee in the proposed bargaining unit is a managerial or confidential position on the grounds that ... 59 (1) ... (c) the occupant of the position provides advice on labour relations, staffing or classification; ... g) the occupant of the position has duties and responsibilities not otherwise described in this subsection and should not be included in a bargaining unit for reasons of conflict of interest or by reason of the person’s duties and responsibilities to the employer; ...

paragraphs.summary: The FPSLRA provisions permit exclusion of positions providing advice on labour relations, staffing, or classification.

propositions.text: The applicant argues that the statutory provisions should be read narrowly to protect the right to unionize.
propositions.quote: the applicant submits that the text, context and purpose of the relevant provisions indicate that Parliament contemplated that all labour relations-related exclusions would fall under either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA and that it was therefore not reasonable to interpret paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Act as including duties in relations to labour relations matters that do not rise to the level of being covered by either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: The applicant claims the adjudicator's reliance on the incumbent's seniority was unreasonable and irrelevant to the duties analysis.
propositions.quote: the applicant asserts that the adjudicator unreasonably premised his decision in large part on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position within the CILP was a senior, experienced lawyer.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues for a narrow interpretation of the provisions and criticizes reliance on the incumbent's seniority.

propositions.text: The court disagrees with the applicant's interpretive and factual arguments.
propositions.quote: With respect, I disagree with both submissions.

propositions.text: The court finds the interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) as reasonable and the reliance on the incumbent's seniority justified.
propositions.quote: The adjudicator’s interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA was therefore reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the applicant's arguments and affirms the reasonableness of the adjudicator's interpretation and findings.

propositions.text: The adjudicator's comments about the incumbent's seniority were contextually appropriate and not the basis of the decision.
propositions.quote: the comments made by the adjudicator in paragraphs 42 and 43 of his reasons that the applicant points to must be read in context and are responsive to suggestions that the employer could have ensured all labour relations-sensitive discussions were held with the more junior excluded lawyer in the CILP.

propositions.text: The adjudicator's decision was not unreasonably based on the incumbent's experience.
propositions.quote: the adjudicator highlights the duties assigned to the LP-04 position that gave rise to a conflict of interest, such as providing advice in respect of privacy or access to information issues in connection with litigation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the adjudicator reasonably based his decision on the duties, not the seniority of the incumbent.

propositions.text: The application is dismissed with costs of $2,500.
propositions.quote: I would accordingly dismiss this application, with costs, fixed in the agreed-upon all-inclusive amount of $2,500.00, which I believe to be reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application and awards costs.
